newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria announces crackdown on police corruption.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria announces crackdown on police corruption.

text.p: Bulgaria's police said on Tuesday they would step up a campaign against corruption in their own ranks and against white-collar crime in the country by recruiting experts in economics, law and computer technology.
"This year police have filed six suits against police officers on suspicion of corruption and another 18 officers were investigated," National Police Director Slavcho Bosilkov told a news conference.
Last year 38 police officers were investigated for corruption and one suit filed, he said.
Crime and corruption have flourished in the seven years since the collapse of communism and the police are poorly paid and badly equipped.

"It is obvious that the only effective way to fight white collar crime is to have young experts in economy, law and computer technologies in the Economic Police Directorate and the National Investigation Service," Bosilkov said.

He said five experts from the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation would arrive on Wednesday to provide technical assistance to the Bulgarian police in investigating tax evasion and misappropriation of funds.
Bulgaria's police prosecuted more than 4,000 economic crimes accounting for some 30.6 billion levs ($19 million) in the first four months of the year, police said.
